claim: AK(n) trivial iff AK(-n-1) trivial. Known-trivial window n = -3..2, so AK(3) and AK(-4) sit just outside it. A uniform shift 1 <= k <= 6 would trivialize the whole AK line.
scope: Fold and finite window check formalized in ACWindow.lean (core Lean 4.29.1, no mathlib).

claim: If p divides one of n-2 .. n+3, AK(n) and (x,y) are AC-equivalent in C_p*C_p. For AK(3): p = 2..6 covered, p = 7 is the first uncovered size.
[1,13,5,11,4,6,3,5,0] reaches (x,y) in C5*C5; radius-4 balls of 13,689 and 4,929 states are disjoint, so 8 moves do not suffice there. In the free group the same moves end at lengths 23 and 35.
scope: Certificate formalized in Lean; ball sizes reproduced by cp5_radius4.py (reported); free-group lengths re-checked in this session.

lane: Spectral gap of the move graph
claim: P = (1/14) sum of the 14 moves; cI <= I-P <= (2-c)I with c = (2-sqrt3)/28 = 0.00957, via squared product moves, a free F2 action on exponent matrices, the 4-regular tree and Kesten's bound.
With g_R = (I-P)^-1 delta_R and loop-weight M: R is AC-trivial iff <g_R, M g_R> > 0.
scope: A reformulation, not an algorithm. The same gap holds on every normally generating class, so the gap alone cannot single out AK(3).
